text:
jordan: Hit a weird p99 on streaming decode. GPU ptr went stale mid-request after compaction moved pages.
lia: Is this soft-offload compaction?
jordan: Yes. Timeline: validate->use->compactor moves->next validate fails, synchronous rebind adds ~20ms.
mike: We should avoid synchronous rebind on hot paths. Two options: short-lived reserve()/release() to prevent compaction, or epoched handles with fast-validate+async-repair.
pat: reserve increases host memory under pressure. Epoch handles sound safer if we design a low-latency fallback (e.g., read-copy from host for one request).
lia: Agree. Also leader election for rebind so only one thread does remap; others wait with deadline then fall back.
jordan: API proposal: reserve(lease_ms)/release(), handle.validate(epoch)->bool, handle.refresh() async. Instrument invalidations/rebind-latency per-tenant.
pat: Compactor must acquire tenant token to bump epoch atomically around move. Document flow in RFC.
infra-bot: canary: deploying "epoch-handles-v0.1" to 5% infra.
mike: Perf targets: read-copy <5ms p99, async full remap <25ms p99. We'll add microbench.
jordan: I'll draft RFC and open PR with microbench link.
lia: Thanks — let's keep the reserve API but make name "reserve" not "pin" to avoid confusion.
